title: Infra: GPU fleet, capacity, cloud accounts, networking, IaC & CI/CD — consolidated playbook
author: Ayesha Kapoor
content:
Summary

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's current runbooks, standards, and operational patterns for GPU fleet capacity, cloud accounts and networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD build pipelines, and day-2 runbooks. It is intended as the single-entry reference for infra engineers and on-call operators executing capacity planning, provisioning, and emergency operations related to GPU-backed inference workloads.

Scope
- GPU fleet sizing and lifecycle (procurement → provisioning → retirement)
- Cloud accounts and networking guardrails for GPU clusters (VPCs, peering, private endpoints)
- Terraform/IaC module patterns and recommended layouts (modules, state, secrets)
- CI/CD patterns for build, image promotion, and infra change gating
- Runbooks for capacity events, rolling upgrades, and incident response

Owner and stakeholders
- Primary owner: infra engineering (platform & gpu-fleet subteam)
- Secondary stakeholders: serving runtime, eng-sre, security, product infra
- Escalation: infra lead -> eng-sre manager -> CTO on >6-hour outages or cross-region data plane failures

High-level architecture and responsibilities
- GPU Fleet: cluster manager (kube-gpu-manager), autoscaler service (autoscaler-api), and node-provisioner (terraform modules + cloud provider images)
- Control plane: centralized control account for global resources (IAM roles, shared VPCs, provider secrets)
- Customer / tenant accounts: per-environment cloud accounts with limited footprint and VPC peering into control plane networks
- IaC: modular Terraform with semantic modules for node pools, GPU images, network constructs, and observability stacks
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions for PR gating and Terraform plan; ArgoCD for cluster-level manifests and image rollouts

1) GPU fleet capacity planning
- SLOs and demand signals:
  - Target pod startup P95: < 45s for warm container images on Dedicated clusters
  - Scaling SLO: node provisioning 95th <= 300s for preemptible spot pools, <= 700s for cold-provisioned reserved instances
  - Cost target: $/vGPU-hour budget tracked per-team and aggregated monthly
- Inputs for capacity planning:
  - Historical token throughput + 95th percentile model length and concurrency by service (source: telemetry-usage reports)
  - Planned model rollouts and expected qps increase (product roadmap inputs)
  - Slacklined headroom for burst (recommended 30% buffer over expected peak)
- Process (quarterly + ad-hoc spikes):
  1. Infra team runs capacity forecast using telemetry and queue-length models (template: capacity-forecast-YYYYMM.xlsx).
  2. Validate with serving-runtime: kernel selection & memory profiles for hot models.
  3. Decide procurement (reserved vs spot) and schedule scaling event.
  4. Create change proposal (TDR) and run through change management (security review if cross-account).

2) Cloud accounts and networking guardrails
- Account topology:
  - control-global (shared IAM, provider secrets, observability sinks)
  - infra-prod (production GPU clusters)
  - infra-staging, infra-dev
  - customer-managed/private accounts (for Private deployments)
- Networking patterns:
  - Shared VPCs for observability/control-plane services; dedicated VPCs for GPU clusters with VPC peering to control-global
  - Use private endpoints for control plane APIs; avoid public IPs on GPU nodes unless explicitly required
  - Egress control: NAT gateway for limited egress; egress allowlist via firewall rules (approved registries, monitoring endpoints)
- Security & IAM:
  - Principle of least privilege for cross-account roles: assume-role with short-lived STS tokens and tight IAM policies
  - KMS key per-account for disk and secrets; customer-managed keys for Private deployments

3) Terraform / IaC modules and state management
- Module patterns (recommended):
  - modules/gpu_node_pool: encapsulates machine type, accelerator config, disk layout, taints/labels, and autoscaler hooks
  - modules/networking: VPC, subnets, route tables, firewall rules, endpoint services
  - modules/cluster_bootstrap: IAM bindings, node image bootstrap scripts, instance templates
  - modules/observability: metrics-forwarder, logging sinks, traces collectors
- State and backends:
  - Remote state in centralized backend (Terraform Cloud or S3 + DynamoDB for locking). Each account/environment has its own state workspace.
  - State encryption using account KMS; state access via dedicated infra service accounts
- Secrets and provider credentials:
  - Provider credentials stored in vault (HashiCorp Vault or cloud secret manager) and referenced via CI vault-plugin
  - Avoid hardcoding provider keys in modules; use assume-role pattern to grant short-lived credentials
- Example usage snippet (module call):
  ```hcl
  module "gpu_node_pool" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-modules.git//modules/gpu_node_pool"
    name   = "gpu-prod-np-1"
    region = "us-west-2"
    machine_type = "n2d-highmem-16"
    accelerators = [{type = "nvidia-a100", count = 1}]
    spot_preference = true
  }
  ```

4) CI/CD and build pipelines
- Pipeline responsibilities:
  - PR validation: linting, plan-only Terraform checks, static analysis (tfsec), unit tests for helper scripts
  - Merge gating: require successful plan + approvers for prod workspace
  - Apply: run by GitHub Actions with tf-apply bot account and Require 2-step approval for infra-prod
  - Image build: cloud-build / GitHub Actions producing signed images, pushed to approved registries only
- Recommended Git branching and workspace mapping:
  - main -> infra-prod workspace (protected, apply via pipeline only)
  - develop -> infra-staging workspace
  - feature/* -> ephemeral workspaces for experimental changes
- CI snippet (example GitHub Actions job for Terraform plan):
  ```yaml
  name: Terraform Plan
  on: [pull_request]
  jobs:
    plan:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: Setup Terraform
          uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
        - name: Install tfsec
          run: curl -sSL https://tfsec.dev/install.sh | bash
        - name: Terraform Init
          run: terraform init -backend-config=\"bucket=${{ secrets.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}\"
        - name: Terraform Plan
          run: terraform plan -no-color -out=plan.out
  ```

5) Runbooks (day-2 ops)
- Runbook: GPU capacity spike (shortages/queue growth):
  1. Triage: check autoscaler logs (autoscaler-api) and node pool state (k8s nodes Ready/NotReady)
  2. Verify spot termination rates and recent provisioning failures in cloud console
  3. If spot interruptions high, switch critical node pools to reserved or increase spot diversification
  4. Evacuate non-critical workloads by applying cordon + drain on lower-priority taints
  5. Open follow-up incident with capacity forecast and remediation (procure more reserved or schedule uplift)
- Runbook: Rolling GPU node pool upgrade:
  1. Create canary node pool with new image and boot scripts
  2. Migrate 5% traffic (use node selectors / deployment affinity) for 24 hours and run smoke tests
  3. If stable, ramp to 25% then 50% then full (30–60min between ramps depending on test coverage)
  4. If regression, rollback: drain new nodes and decommission canary; create rollback ticket and postmortem

6) Monitoring, SLOs, and alerts
- Key metrics to track:
  - Node-level: pod startup latency, GPU utilization, GPU memory pressure, node provisioning latency
  - Control-plane: Terraform apply failures, remote state errors, provider rate-limit errors
  - Cost: $/vGPU-hour per cluster, %spot usage, monthly forecast vs actual
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - GPU memory pressure > 85% on >20% of nodes for 10m -> P1 oncall
  - Node provisioning 95th > 900s -> P2 (investigate cloud quotas / image pipeline)
  - Terraform plan drift detection (unexpected drift) -> P2 owner: infra-IaC

7) Cost and procurement guidance
- Spot vs reserved strategy:
  - Primary: use spot for non-critical and training/sandbox clusters with graceful eviction handlers
  - Reserve pool for latency-sensitive production workloads (Redwood Dedicated critical pools)
- Sizing heuristics:
  - Default headroom: 30% CPU/GPU buffer above forecasted 95th qps
  - For models with large KV caches, add additional memory headroom per node (documented in model-onboarding)

8) Change control and postmortems
- All infra-prod changes require: CI plan, one infra approver, and at least one stakeholder approval from serving-runtime if the change affects model-serving labels or kernel selection
- Post-incident process: create postmortem within 72 hours, include root cause analysis, mitigation, and owner for follow-up action items (tracked in eng-platform backlog)

9) Templates, CLI tools, and common commands
- Common commands:
  - Validate TF: terraform fmt && terraform validate
  - Remote plan: TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE=infra-prod make tf-plan
  - Reprovision node pool: ./scripts/reprovision-node-pool.sh --pool gpu-prod-np-1 --region us-west-2
- Template checklist for node-pool PR:
  - [ ] Module changes covered by unit tests
  - [ ] TF plan reviewed and no destructive changes to prod node pools
  - [ ] Observability changes included (metrics, logs)
  - [ ] Rollout plan with canary periods described

Appendix A — Example TF module inputs table
| input | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| name | resource prefix | gpu-prod-np-1 |
| region | cloud region | us-west-2 |
| machine_type | machine family | a2-highmem-16 |
| accelerators | GPU type/count | [{type = \"nvidia-a100\", count = 1}] |
| spot_preference | prefer spot | true |

Appendix B — Escalation matrix
- Oncall infra engineer (P0/P1) -> infra lead (P1/P2) -> eng-sre manager (P2) -> CTO (P0 extended)

Related reading and links

- gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026: canonical runbooks for day-2 ops
- infra-gpu-fleet-capacity-ci-cd-iac-playbook-2026: templates and CI examples

Maintaining this doc
- Owner must review quarterly and after any major incident impacting GPU capacity.
- Submit edits as PRs against the docs repo. Changes that alter runbook steps require a reviewer from eng-sre and serving-runtime.

End of playbook
